Here is a comprehensive report of all findings across the seven search areas.

---

## 1. Top-Performing Open-Source Models for Autoformalization (May 2026)

**StepFun-Formalizer-32B** is the current SOTA for dedicated autoformalization:
- **40.5% BEq@1** on FormalMATH-Lite
- **26.7% BEq@1** on ProverBench
- Training pipeline: 2-stage SFT (formal knowledge distillation with 183K Lean4-aligned pairs from NuminaMath via Kimina-Autoformalizer-7B, plus 5.8K template-guided reasoning trajectories from Claude 3.7) followed by RLVR (BEq-based reward using GRPO + DAPO)
- Published at AAAI; open-weight model on HuggingFace (`stepfun-ai/StepFun-Formalizer-32B`)

**Kimina-Autoformalizer-7B** (from the Numina/Kimi team):
- Used for data synthesis (the 183K pairs that StepFun-Formalizer trains on)
- Kimina-Prover (the prover side) achieves 80.7% pass@8192 on miniF2F and 48.94% Pass@3200 on FormalMATH-Lite

**DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B** (primarily a prover, but includes autoformalization via subgoal decomposition):
- 88.9% pass ratio on MiniF2F-test
- 49/658 problems from PutnamBench
- Uses recursive decomposition where DeepSeek-V3 produces natural-language-to-Lean-4 subgoal chains

**InternLM2-StepProver-7B**:
- MiniF2F-test: 54.5%, ProofNet: 18.1%, Putnam: 5 problems
- Fine-tuned on 29K theorems from 100+ Lean 4 repos and Lean-Workbook

**DeepSeek-Math-V2** (released Jan 2026):
- Built on DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-Base, 128K context window
- Gold-level on IMO 2025, near-perfect 118/120 on Putnam 2024
- Generator-verifier architecture for self-correcting proofs

**Practical autoformalization** (non-specialized): ChatGPT 5.2 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 running in feedback loops with proof checkers have produced 130K+ lines of formal topology in ~2 weeks for ~$100.

---

## 2. Top Open-Source Models for Mathematical Reasoning (Base Models for Fine-Tuning)

**DeepSeek-R1**: Leading open-source reasoning model, competitive with o1-level reasoning. MIT-licensed.

**DeepSeek-V3.2**: MIT-licensed. GPQA Diamond: 68.2%, MATH-500: 82.7%. Outperforms V3.1 on mixed reasoning and agent tasks.

**Qwen2.5-Math-72B-Instruct**: Best open-source math-specialized model. Outperforms Qwen2-Math-72B-Instruct by 4.4 points (English) and 6.1 points (Chinese). Also has 7B and 1.5B variants. Supports CoT and Tool-integrated Reasoning.

**Qwen3.7-Max-Preview** (May 2026): Elo 1,475 in Arena, ranked #7 in math.

**Qwen3.5**: Newer Qwen series model available in 2026.

**Other notable models**: MiniMax-M1-80k, Kimi-Dev-72B, THUDM/GLM-Z1-9B-0414 (lightweight).

**Best candidates for autoformalization fine-tuning base**: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (already demonstrated by FormaRL), Qwen2.5-Math-72B, or DeepSeek-V3.2 derivatives.

---

## 3. Baseline Numbers to Beat on FormalMATH and ProofNet

### FormalMATH (5,560 Lean4 problems, high-school to undergraduate)
- **FormalMATH-Full (Pass@32)**: Best model Kimina-Prover achieves only **16.46%**
- **FormalMATH-Lite** (425-problem subset):
  - StepFun-Formalizer-32B: **40.5% BEq@1** (SOTA for autoformalization)
  - STP: 53.17% Pass@3200
  - DeepSeek-V1.5-RL: 50.35% Pass@3200
  - Kimina-Prover-7B: 48.94% Pass@3200
  - DeepSeek-V1.5-SFT: 46.82% Pass@3200

### ProofNet (371 examples, undergraduate-level, Lean 3)
- Code-davinci-002 baseline: **12.9%** (in-context learning)
- GPT-4 (50 samples): **45.1%** (up from 31.0% single-shot)
- FormaRL (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B): **26.15% pass@1** (up from 4.04% baseline)
- InternLM2-StepProver: **18.1%**

### Key insight from FormalMATH
A counterintuitive inverse relationship was found: natural-language solution guidance *hurts* formal proof success. Naive CoT outperforms NL-augmented CoT.

---

## 4. FormaRL -- VERIFIED

- **Paper**: "FormaRL: Enhancing Autoformalization with no Labeled Data"
- **arXiv**: [2508.18914](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18914)
- **Venue**: Accepted at **COLM 2025** (confirmed via GitHub repo tag `[COLM25]`)
- **GitHub**: [THUNLP-MT/FormaRL](https://github.com/THUNLP-MT/FormaRL)
- **Method**: Uses GRPO algorithm with dual reward: (1) Lean compiler syntax check + (2) LLM-based consistency/semantic check. Requires only 859 unlabeled data points.
- **Results**:
  - Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct pass@1: **4.04% -> 26.15%** on ProofNet (4-6x improvement)
  - Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct pass@1: **2.4% -> 9.6%** on uproof
  - Out-of-distribution (uproof): pass@1 6.2% -> 9.6%, pass@16 24.4% -> 33.6%

---

## 5. DDR (Direct Dependency Retrieval) -- VERIFIED

- **Paper**: "Improving Autoformalization Using Direct Dependency Retrieval"
- **arXiv**: [2511.11990](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11990)
- **Also published at ICLR 2025** as "Rethinking and Improving Autoformalization: Towards a Faithful Metric and a Dependency Retrieval-based Approach"
- **Method**: Uses SAC (Search-Augment-Construct) to build a dependency retrieval dataset of **500K+ samples**. The DDR model directly generates candidate library dependencies from NL descriptions, then verifies existence in the formal library.
- **Results**: Significantly outperforms SOTA in both retrieval precision and recall. Autoformalizers equipped with DDR show consistent advantages in both single-attempt accuracy and multi-attempt stability vs. traditional selection-based RAG.

---

## 6. DRIFT -- VERIFIED

- **Paper**: "DRIFT: Decompose, Retrieve, Illustrate, then Formalize Theorems"
- **arXiv**: [2510.10815](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10815)
- **Method**: 4-stage pipeline: (1) Decompose informal statement into atomic concept-focused sub-queries, (2) Retrieve foundational premises from Mathlib, (3) Retrieve illustrative theorems, (4) Formalize.
- **Results**:
  - ProofNet: **+13.34 F1 points** over baseline, nearly doubling DPR baseline F1
  - Claude-Opus-4 achieves highest F1 on ProofNet at **27.68%** with DRIFT
  - MiniF2F-test: +2.08 F1 points over baseline
  - ConNF: +7.74 F1 points over baseline

---

## 7. CRAMF -- VERIFIED

- **Paper**: "Automated Formalization via Conceptual Retrieval-Augmented LLMs"
- **arXiv**: [2508.06931](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06931)
- **OpenReview**: Available
- **Method**: Automatically constructs a concept-definition knowledge base from Mathlib4, indexing **26,000+ formal definitions** and **1,000+ core mathematical concepts**. Uses contextual query augmentation with domain/application-level signals and dual-channel hybrid retrieval with reranking.
- **Results**: Tested on miniF2F, ProofNet, and a new AdvancedMath benchmark. Achieves up to **62.1%** and average **29.9% relative improvement** in translation accuracy.

---

| FormalMATH-Full | Pass@32 | 16.46% | Kimina-Prover |
